requirement: Serve documents with a strong version ETag and accept replacements only when If-Match names the current version, answering 428 when the header is missing, 412 when it is stale or weak, and 404 for unknown documents, bumping the version on success.
skeleton: DocIn and DocOut pydantic models, DOCS state with reset_db, etag formatting a quoted version, load raising 404, a GET handler setting ETag, and a PUT handler checking If-Match before writing a new version.
caption: Optimistic concurrency in FastAPI with entity tags. DocIn is a pydantic model with a title of 1 to 200 characters and DocOut adds an integer version; DOCS holds one seeded draft at version 1. etag(doc) returns a strong tag such as quoted v1. load(doc_id) raises HTTPException 404 for unknown ids. GET /docs/{doc_id} returns the document and sets the ETag response header. PUT /docs/{doc_id} reads If-Match through Annotated Header; when it is absent it raises HTTPException 428 saying the If-Match header is required, and when the stripped value differs from the current strong tag, including a weak W/ tag, it raises HTTPException 412 saying the document changed and naming the current version. Otherwise it stores a new DocOut with the new title and the version plus one, sets the new ETag and returns it. The fixture asserts that GET returns version 1 with ETag v1, that a PUT with v1 returns version 2 and ETag v2, that a second PUT still sending v1 gets 412 naming version 2 and leaves the first update in place, that a PUT without If-Match gets 428, that a weak tag gets 412, and that an unknown document gets 404.

plan.intent: Stop concurrent editors from silently overwriting each other
constraints: Reads and successful writes carry a strong ETag of the version
Stale or weak If-Match raises HTTPException 412 and changes nothing
Each successful write increments the version

rationale.teaches: Version-based strong ETags compared against If-Match, with distinct 428 and 412 responses.
rationale.why: Treating a missing header as permission, accepting weak tags, or forgetting to bump the version all let a single editor succeed, so the fixture replays a stale tag after another write.

ops.docstring: Documents updated under optimistic locking with If-Match and version ETags.

ops.stmt: from fastapi import FastAPI, Header, HTTPException, Response, status

params.name: DocOut
params.doc: A stored document and its version.

ops.source:
def reset_db() -> None:
    """Restore the single seed document."""
    DOCS.clear()
    DOCS[1] = DocOut(title="Draft", version=1)

candidates.why_wrong: A request without If-Match is accepted, so blind overwrites are still possible.
The weak prefix is stripped before comparing, so weak tags pass a strong precondition.
The version never increments, so a stale tag keeps matching after other writes.
A stale tag answers 409 instead of the 412 precondition failure clients expect.
The PUT response omits the new ETag, so the client cannot chain its next update.
